hints.title: Rightmost Silhouette Obstacle
hints.text: Looking at the tree from the right side reveals the rightmost node of each vertical level. How can a level-by-level traversal capture the last element of every tier directly?

hints.title: Tier Silhouette Invariant
hints.text: The right side view consists of exactly the last node encountered at each level during a standard left-to-right tier traversal.

hints.title: Level-by-Level Capture Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return an empty list. Maintain a queue for level-by-level traversal. For each tier of size k, dequeue all k nodes, enqueue children from left to right, and record the value of the kth node into the answer array.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 100)
W: maximum level width of tree
complexity.notes: Breadth-first search extracting the rightmost element per tier in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simply traversing right child pointers misses left children that become visible when right subtrees are shorter.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Auxiliary queue memory proportional to maximum width W.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that left subtrees can protrude deeper than right subtrees.
